cands.name: Scott Alan Meyers

money.note: Individuals gave $19,161; PAC money $350; candidate's own money $98,800. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Attorney with about 37 years in civil law practice, self-employed for 26 years. Graduated from Pepperdine University School of Law in 1988. Republican candidate for California's 30th Congressional District in 2026. The sources reviewed list no elected office.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California, plus several voter-guide recommendations listed by Ballotpedia (including The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn).

His campaign site lists the California Republican Party, L.A. County Republican Party, Reform California and California Young Republicans, along with individuals including Dr. Houman Hemmati and Jennifer Van Laar of Red State.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birth city or year. We found no elected or governmental office held, so there is no voting record. We found no documented stance from him on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buyers, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay. His immigration position is limited to a general "secure the border" statement. We found no news coverage of controversies and no foreign ties.

cands.bio: Democrat representing California's 30th District in the U.S. House since January 2025. Former film and TV development executive and producer, and owner of an art glass dealership. Glendale City Council member 2009–2016 (mayor 2011–2012), then California Assembly member 2016–2024.

endorsements.text: California Democratic Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, Equality California, and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter endorsed her 2026 campaign, along with YIMBY Action.
Her campaign site lists endorsements from Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Giffords PAC, League of Conservation Voters, SEIU California and Abundant Housing Los Angeles, among others.

cands.gaps: We found no stated position or record from her on data centers, eliminating homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, police pay and pensions, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay. Where she grew up is not documented in the pages we reviewed. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We found no documented controversies, foreign-government ties or specific data-center or land-use stances in the sources provided. Her Assembly record on housing, parking and growth was not detailed enough to show how she acted on slowing growth or protecting land.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her 2024 campaign website said she has worked to "cut red tape that has prevented the development of housing" and to increase affordable housing stock.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she named "restoring a woman's right to choose" as a policy priority, and her campaign site lists protecting reproductive freedom.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she led efforts as an Assembly member to prevent gun violence, and her 2024 survey cites banning gun shows on Glendale city property.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act, which requires DHS to detain certain undocumented immigrants arrested for theft-related offenses; it passed the House 263-156 and became law in January 2025.
